name: Salsify
grown_as: Salsify (oyster plant), a biennial grown for its long thin root, lifted in its first autumn and winter. Plants left in flower the next spring; the flower buds and young shoots are eaten too.
habit: Year 1: an upright tuft of long grass-like grey-green leaves 30 to 45 cm. Year 2: a smooth, little-branched flowering stem 60 to 120 cm with grass-like leaves clasping it, each branch ending in one flower head. Milky sap in all parts.

leaf.arrangement: A tuft from the root top; alternate up the stem
leaf.outline: Long and narrow (linear), 20 to 40 cm by 0.5 to 1.5 cm, widest at the base and tapering steadily to a long fine point
leaf.base: Broad, wrapping and clasping the stem or crown
leaf.tip: Long, very fine point, often curling
leaf.veins: Parallel veins along the leaf, with a pale keel down the middle
leaf.surface: Smooth, hairless, with a grey waxy bloom; folded a little along the midrib

flower.form: A dandelion-like head made only of strap-shaped florets, with long narrow green bracts sticking out well beyond the florets like the points of a star
flower.petals: Many strap-shaped florets, each ending in five tiny teeth
flower.centre: The inner florets darker; dark purple-brown anther tubes
flower.behind: 8 (sometimes 5 to 10) long narrow green bracts in one row, 1.5 to 2 times as long as the florets
flower.carried: One head at the tip of each stem, facing up, on a stalk that is swollen and club-shaped just below the head. Open in the morning, closed by midday
flower.size: 4 to 6 cm across including the bracts
flower.season: May to July of the second year

fruit: A very large, round 'clock' 8 to 12 cm across, like a giant dandelion clock, of long-beaked seeds each topped by a feathery pale brown parachute whose hairs are interwoven into a web.
seedling: Two long, narrow, grass-like seed leaves 3 to 6 cm, grey-green, then grass-like true leaves.
winter: The leaves die back in hard frost to a small tuft at the crown; roots are left in the ground and lifted as needed. New leaves appear in early spring.

leaf: long narrow grass-like leaf tapering to a fine point
bloom: a head of purple strap-shaped florets only, no central disc
long narrow green bracts reaching well beyond the florets in a star
a swollen stalk just below the head
seed: a long slim ribbed brown seed with a long beak, 2 to 3 cm
a feathery parachute on the beak, or bare if rubbed off
young: an upright tuft of grey-green grass-like leaves
crop: a long thin pale cream-brown root, 2 to 3 cm thick and 20 to 30 cm long
many fine side rootlets along it
a tuft of grass-like leaves on top
flower: a tall smooth stem with clasping grass-like leaves
purple flower heads, one per branch tip, with long star-like bracts
seedhead: a large round clock of feathery parachutes on long beaks
the green bracts spread or turned down below

look_alikes: Goat's-beard (Tragopogon pratensis) is the wild cousin, with yellow heads. Scorzonera has broader leaves, yellow heads with short bracts and a black root. Grasses and leeks lack the milky sap.
